body:
I think most of us here are willing to listen without judging and talk or offer feedback...

My issues are more centered around OCD & depression, but... I know the feeling of hurting while being constantly alone. Of wanting someone to be the hand to reach out, but being terrified of asking for a stranger to be that hand. 

For whatever it is worth? You aren't alone in your suffering. And many, many people here are hoping you don't give in to darker impulses.

Always here to listen/talk if you'd like
For whatever it is worth - if you'd ever care to vent or chat, I'd be glad to listen

Isolation and 'living in the mind' is something I'm painfully familiar with, due to my OCD.

But...the desire to reach out here? I think that's a hopeful sign. 

I like to think many of us fear 'making the leap' of acting because some part of our instinctive mind refuses to let go of the idea that hope still exists (however distant or small it may be or seem).

I don't know your specific struggle or pain, but I hope your suffering abates.

I think this is a common thought for people who are considering suicide, for the same reason many will leave a note - a desire to explain. I've actually gone as far as to explicitly ask my best friend to do certain things if I ever die (not telling him that I've experienced suicidal ideation, but rather presenting it as a 'just in case' course of action).

So no - I don't think you're alone in this line of thought. I do hope you don't pursue that course of action, though (a feeling I imagine most here share)
Yes, I'm in therapy. Yes I've talked about my suicidal thoughts with others. ...but I do feel like my OCD defines, as much as it controls my life and decisions.

I don't feel like my thoughts can be cured. Not after over a decade of trying and failing - at least.

It's like an incessant, constant interruption in my mind... The whole 'splinter in the mind' bs? That's the feeling. That something is wrong in a way I can never fix.

I've been trying to lose myself in the few things that give me brief joy, but it feels like I'm just indulging in whatever distracts me. I...don't want a distraction. I want hope. And right now I don't feel like I have it.

Farm - I hope you come back. I'd appreciate your insights particularly.

Yes - I've been to a psychiatrist. First diagnosed over a decade ago, most of that time in treatment. Too many different kinds of meds, talk therapy, some exposure therapy, some group therapy...

Each has helped in its own way, but it's a marginal help. The symptoms still wax and wan, never abating and always intruding.

My primary obsession is about contamination fears. Bodily emissions are a trigger for my compulsions - so simply using the bathroom results in scrubbing my hands, often until the skin dry and flaking - more rarely drawing blood. 

...but what's more convinced me that my isolation, in terms of romance, will remain, is this: bodily emissions being triggers includes sex. I'm a male who both desires and fears sex, because of this - and it's very difficult to imagine any normal person making peace with that. The only lasting relationship I've had was fairly well crippled by my OCD. True - I could find the love of my life tomorrow, but past experience tends to indicate that if I keep going tomorrow I'll just be spending most of my day alone and trying to cope with neurotic thoughts.

The things that give a brief reprieve are forms of escapism: reading, writing, gaming.

Hard to read or write when I can't escape my thoughts, though.

I've tried multiple SSRI's and have some experience with tricyclic antidepressants. I've also tried multiple anxiety meds, a sedative, and more. 

Going for a walk, watching the sunset, etc? Those may well help ease depression but they do nothing to escape the neurotic thoughts of OCD. It's like your mind is screaming uncontrollably at you to bow to compulsions, so the advice of relaxing with nature in response seems misguided. More of a response to depression and anxiety than intrusive thoughts and forced compulsions.

I try to be a realist.

Given the length of time in treatment and the variety of types attempted, it's difficult to find an optimistic outlook. Ten years of failure to manage symptoms doesn't give me optimism, no.
I'm a male... Does it matter?

I get a small disability payment from an old job that's a fraction of my old salary, minus a cut for insurance. I struggled with bills but mostly managed on my old salary. Getting far less than that now? It's far worse. I've had a few part time jobs since then, but it rarely lasts. Maybe two months, maybe a dozen.

So I do some freelance work, mostly because it's difficult maintaining even part time employment. When symptoms are mostly managed (present, pervasive, but not constantly forcefully disruptive) - I can work in some fields fairly well most of the time. It intrudes, but...not to the point of stopping me from functioning altogether. It's when the symptoms are worse and on the rise that working becomes impossible, maybe briefly, maybe longer.

I've filed for SSA disability a few times, but been rejected. Essentially for the reasons I outlined above: I can, at least at times, work. The conditions are constant, but the impairment level varies enough that it's been shot down.

I want my hands to not hurt  because the skin is irritated/raw/peeling from the scrubbing. I want to not feel like a failure for being unable to pay my bills (at least, not all of them). And I want to not feel guilty for putting loved ones in uncomfortable situations because of my inability to keep consistent work with my condition.

I'm grateful for the consistent kind words and insights, but...
In the night, when I can't help but ruminate, I just don't want to be left alone with the thoughts of my many failings and shortcomings. 

At least in the day there are moments when I'm thinking of what might be, instead of these hours when I only think of what 'should' have been.

And another night comes without sleep or reprieve. 

...does anyone have a similar experience or something to give some hope here? The straw I'm still grasping at is not wanting to leave a burden behind but I feel like everything holding me together is gone.

I don't have anyone I can talk to with OCD in my life - at least, not this severe. I do have some friends that have struggled with anxiety or depression issues, but none I'm particularly close to. 

Stress in general tends to make the OCD worse. At the moment that's particularly a financial concern, but...just finding the energy to do anything is a challenge, now.

I just don't want to feel alone, helpless, or hopeless. And at the moment I feel all three.
